answer: Ephemeral task-seeded keying. Each identity must solve a fresh, randomly generated problem whose answer is embedded in a one-time token; the token seeds a keypair accepted only for that task. At the wharf, agents submit tokens that expire within minutes. Reusing an answer is rejected because the token binds to a nonce and timestamp, so replay fails. An attacker must compute each answer independently, paying full cost per identity per task, plus the ember of compute wasted on expired submissions. The orchard of valid tokens thus grows only through real work,
